title: King's Indian Defense: Mar del Plata Variation
line: The center locks. White attacks on the queen's side, and Black storms the king.

steps.text: The King's Indian Defense: White builds a big center, and Black's bishop waits on the long diagonal.
Both sides castle, and Black strikes at the center with the pawn in front of its king. This is the main line.
Bring the other knight out. It attacks White's pawn on d4 a second time.
steps.after: White pushes past and closes the center.

steps.text: The knight is attacked. Step it back toward the king's side, where Black will attack.

wrong.c6a5: On the edge the knight has no safe way back, and White's pawn on b2 comes forward to trap it.

steps.after: White's knight steps back to make room for its pawns.

steps.text: Move the other knight back too. It clears the way for the pawn on f7.

also.f6e8: That clears the way too. This lesson goes on with the knight to the other square.

steps.text: Push the pawn on f7 two squares. It attacks White's pawn on e4.
Push it once more. It attacks the bishop and gains space next to White's king.
Bring the next pawn along. Black's pawns march at White's king.
steps.after: A race: White pushes for a break on the other wing, Black goes for the king. Whoever gets there first usually decides the game.

summary: With the center locked, each side attacks where its pawns point: Black at the king, White on the other wing.
